summary: Bulk embedding import from customer causing upstream runtime exits and API gateway error flood
description:
Issue summary:
Customer LexiSearch reports a sharp increase in server errors during a scheduled bulk embedding import. API gateway responded with a high percentage of 5xx codes while upstream runtimes for the customer's dedicated pool were repeatedly exiting.

Impact:
- ~12% of requests for LexiSearch in us-east-1 observed 5xx responses over a ~30 minute window.
- Long polling/streaming sessions for active users disconnected repeatedly.
- Customer reports degraded application behavior (search index not updated).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool for LexiSearch (dedicated tier) in prod-us-east.
- Import was a single multi-part upload containing ~1.2M vectors in 8k chunk batches against embedder-v2-quant.

Steps to reproduce (as reported / reproducible pattern):
1) Schedule a large embedding import using the bulk-upload endpoint with parallel multipart workers (N=16).
2) Workers issue many concurrent generate/embed calls after upload completes.
3) Within minutes, API gateway error rate climbs and upstream runtime processes begin to exit.

Observed logs / metrics:
- apigw.error_rate by tenant spiked to 12% (502/504/500 mix) at 2026-03-13T18:12Z.
- runtime supervisor logs show repeated process exits with stack traces pointing to NVMe I/O timeouts and heavy page fault counts.
- dstat/iostat show NVMe avg await rising from <2ms to >120ms during the window.
- kernel logs include repeated block layer timeouts and mq-deadline warnings.
- pod/container restart count increased by 5x for the dedicated pool.

Preliminary customer impact note: LexiSearch's search ingestion pipeline delayed ~45 minutes and several API calls from their frontend returned errors, causing partial site outages for customers.
comments: Support (2026-03-13T18:25Z) - Aisha Malik: Acknowledged with customer, opened incident. Routed to SRE for immediate mitigation. Asked customer to pause further uploads.

SRE (2026-03-13T18:34Z) - Ben Carroll: Observed I/O latency spike on NVMe backing dedicated pool. Temporarily rate-limiting incoming embed jobs for LexiSearch and draining new sessions to lower-priority nodes. Noted runtime exits correlated with high iowait and kernel block timeouts.
Customer (2026-03-13T18:46Z) - Maria Chen (LexiSearch): Confirmed pause of new imports. Asked for ETA on when normal traffic can resume; they have a business SLA for search freshness.

SRE (2026-03-13T19:05Z) - Ben Carroll: Applied edge throttling for bulk-upload endpoint for tenant, and adjusted node-level i/o scheduling settings (reduced writeback aggressive flushing). Error rate dropped to ~2% but still seeing occasional runtime restarts. Continuing to monitor.

Support (2026-03-13T20:10Z) - Aisha Malik: Updated customer on temporary mitigation and next steps: longer term fix underway with infra to repro in staging and tune autoscaler/backpressure. Customer accepted temporary mitigation and requested postmortem.

SRE (2026-03-14T09:30Z) - Ben Carroll: Reproduced load in staging with synthetic multi-part upload and observed NVMe queuing under parallelism >8. Created repro harness and linked PR to add backpressure at ingest and fail-fast behavior for oversized batches.
Engineering (2026-03-14T11:02Z) - Priya Gupta: Noted change required in runtime to detect sustained iowait and reject new sessions earlier. Preparing a patch and test plan.
investigation: Timeline correlation shows apigw error uptick directly after the customer's parallel workers completed initial uploads and began high-concurrency embed calls.
Hardware metrics implicate the NVMe storage layer: queue depth and await increased dramatically during the window, leading to block layer timeouts and kernel warnings.

Runtime exits align with I/O stalls rather than pure memory OOMs. Process stack traces include syscall wait states and heavy synchronous disk writes from checkpointing/flushing logic inside the embedder runtime.
Autoscaler did not pre-warm additional nodes because the ingest pattern appeared as short-lived high-concurrency bursts; current scaling thresholds are too conservative for large rapid imports.
Edge/APIGW retry behavior amplified load during the first minutes, increasing concurrent inflight to upstream and worsening I/O contention.
Repro in staging succeeds when running 12+ parallel upload workers with similar vector counts; reducing parallelism to <=6 avoids the pathological I/O behavior.
Related linked ticket SUP-472901 documents a prior NVMe iowait incident in a different tenant with similar characteristics (large concurrent jobs).
temporary_workaround: Applied tenant-scoped rate limit to bulk-upload and embed endpoints; gated new embed sessions behind a queuing/token bucket. Adjusted node i/o scheduler tunables and disabled aggressive background writeback on impacted nodes. Customer paused imports during mitigation.
next_steps: Merge engineering patch to implement early backpressure/fail-fast on the embedder when sustained iowait detected (PR linked).
Tune autoscaler to pre-warm nodes for detected large import jobs and add burst capacity policy for dedicated pools.
Add an ingest-side client guidance document recommending max parallelism and chunk size for bulk imports; add service-side soft limits to prevent destructive patterns.
Run a controlled chaos/repro test in staging across dedicated hardware profiles to validate fixes and monitor NVMe metrics.
resolution: Mitigation in place (edge throttling + node i/o adjustments). Engineering patch in progress; monitoring shows error rate reduced to baseline for LexiSearch. Postmortem scheduled and will include client guidance and autoscaler changes.
root_cause: High-concurrency bulk-embedding import caused sustained NVMe queuing and kernel block timeouts on dedicated nodes. Amplified by edge retry amplification and conservative autoscaler thresholds, causing runtime processes to exit and API gateway to return elevated errors.
postmortem_plan: Formal postmortem to be authored once engineering patch is validated in staging. Will include timeline, corrective actions, and customer communication draft. Target publication: 2026-03-20.
